articles.title: Crude oil extends losses despite no changes in the Middle East; demand concerns could be the culprit
articles.description: Crude oil extended the losses over the APAC session despite no change in the US-Iran situation. The only reason I can see for such price action is growth concerns starting to weigh on the demand outlook. This is also what we’ve been seeing with copper as the metal has been selling off hard for several weeks. I’m not sure we are there yet but given that you have to consider both demand and supply, there is certainly a scenario where oil prices could fall without a change in the US-Iran situation. On the news side, military tensions continue to escalate, with a US military source confirming strikes on a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in response to alleged Iranian aggression. Iran then claimed attacks on US air-defence systems at Kuwait's base, while Kuwait and Bahrain reported hostile drone activity and explosions. Meanwhile, the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, although the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a Houthi cruise missile targeting Riyadh. On the negotiations front, there has been no breakthrough, with officials saying Iran has hardened its position following the Republican losses in the US midterm elections. However, US-Qatar discussions were described as extremely positive and constructive. Overall,the situation remains unchanged, with diplomatic efforts continuing without any meaningful breakthrough yet. It goes without saying that a breakthrough would trigger a significant selloff and take oil prices back to pre-war levels relatively quickly. But as of now, this scenario doesn’t look likely. An escalation or a prolonged stalemate should keep oil prices supported, although there’s also a chance that Trump decides to proceed with limited strikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities before exiting the war, which could lead to a temporary spike before a selloff. CRUDE OIL TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that crude oil(CFD contract) dropped to new lows despite no changes on the US-Iran front. The natural target for the sellers should be the 80.00 handle. If the price gets there, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a rally into the 110.00 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to increase the bearish bets into the 68.00 support next. CRUDE OIL TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, we can see the price retested the broken upward trendline before falling to new lows. We have now a downward trendline defining the bearish structure. If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to position for a drop into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 110.00 level next, with the 92.50 level as the first target. ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum on this timeframe. The sellers will likely lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break to extend the pullback into the next trendline. The red lines define the average daily range for today. UPCOMING CATALYSTS Todaywe have the FOMC meeting minutes. Tomorrow, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on US-Iran developments. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.
